title: Balance seesaw and center of mass

data.title: Balance seesaw and center of mass
data.statement:
Given an ASCII drawing of a seesaw, calculate its <<relative center of mass>> and determine whether it is in balance.

The drawing has [[h]] rows and [[w]] columns. Each {{#}} represents a block of the same mass. Blocks are stacked on a continuous surface, which is also made of {{#}} blocks. The last drawing row contains the support {{X}}. Spaces and the support {{X}} have no mass.

The <<relative center of mass>> is the average column index of all {{#}} characters minus the column index of the support {{X}}. Count each {{#}} separately, including multiple blocks in the same column. Vertical positions do not affect this average.

Negative values are to the left of the support {{X}}, and positive values are to the right. A value of {{0}} means the center of mass is aligned with the support {{X}}.

The seesaw is in balance when the relative center of mass is between {{-0.5}} and {{0.5}}, <<including both endpoints>>. Determine balance using the exact value, before rounding it for output.

Output the relative center of mass and the balance result.
data.constraints:
2 ≤ [[h]] ≤ 100
1 ≤ [[w]] ≤ 500
The complete input contains at most {{10000}} characters.
The first [[h]] − {{1}} drawing rows contain only {{#}} and spaces.
Drawing row [[h]] − {{1}} is a continuous surface of one or more {{#}} characters, optionally surrounded by spaces.
Drawing row [[h]] contains exactly one {{X}} and otherwise only spaces.
Every {{#}} above the surface has another {{#}} directly below it.
The {{X}} is directly below a {{#}} of the surface.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Given an ASCII drawing of a seesaw, calculate its relative center of mass and determine whether it is in balance.

The drawing has h rows and w columns. Each # represents a block of the same mass. Blocks are stacked on a continuous surface, which is also made of # blocks. The last drawing row contains the support X. Spaces and the support X have no mass.

The relative center of mass is the average column index of all # characters minus the column index of the support X. Count each # separately, including multiple blocks in the same column. Vertical positions do not affect this average.

Negative values are to the left of the support X, and positive values are to the right. A value of 0 means the center of mass is aligned with the support X.

The seesaw is in balance when the relative center of mass is between -0.5 and 0.5, including both endpoints. Determine balance using the exact value, before rounding it for output.

Output the relative center of mass and the balance result.
Input
Line 1: Two space-separated integers h and w, the height and width of the drawing.
Next h lines: A string line of exactly w characters containing one drawing row. Drawing rows are numbered from 1 to h.
Output
Line 1: The relative center of mass, rounded to exactly six decimal places. Use . as the decimal separator and include trailing zeros.
Line 2: In balance if the exact relative center of mass is between -0.5 and 0.5, including both endpoints. Otherwise, Not in balance.
Constraints
2 ≤ h ≤ 100
1 ≤ w ≤ 500
The complete input contains at most 10000 characters.
The first h − 1 drawing rows contain only # and spaces.
Drawing row h − 1 is a continuous surface of one or more # characters, optionally surrounded by spaces.
Drawing row h contains exactly one X and otherwise only spaces.
Every # above the surface has another # directly below it.
The X is directly below a # of the surface.
Example
Input
4 21
#                    
#####            ####
#####################
         X
Output
0.483871
In balance
